messages:
sarah: quick check — I'm landing a refactor that splits `module/legacy_db` into `module/db-core` + `module/db-connector`. main change: provider usage moves from implicit provider in module to explicit provider aliases. planning `state mv` for the connector resources + update secret paths. pls shout if this will break staging deploys

arun: heads up — that provider alias change can make the lockfile churn. did you update `required_providers` in the module roots? Also pinging @javi for any k8s secret path implications :eyes:

javi: thanks for the ping. the k8s manifests expect secrets at `secrets/db/credentials` envFrom. if you change the Terraform-managed secret key name we need a middleware shim or a rollout plan. can you paste the secret resource snippet?

sarah: snippet below — I moved to explicit alias and changed name to `redwood/db-conn` (was `legacy_db/creds`):
```hcl
provider "kubernetes" {
  alias = "db"
  config_path = var.kubeconfig
}
resource "kubernetes_secret" "db_creds" {
  metadata {
    name = "redwood-db-conn"
    namespace = var.namespace
  }
  data = { username = var.username, password = var.password }
}
```

javi: ok that will change the secret name. we should either: 1) write a short migration job that copies `legacy_db/creds` -> `redwood-db-conn` in staging, or 2) keep the TF resource name same but add a `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata] }` temporarily. I'd vote migration job for clarity.

liz: question on state mv — are you planning `terraform state mv` per workspace? need playbook for the infra oncall to avoid accidental drifts. if you can add the exact `state mv` commands we can run it in a maintenance window.

sarah: yes — plan is per-workspace. intended commands (staging example):
```bash
# move connector resources into new module path
terraform state mv 'module.legacy_db.module.connector.kubernetes_secret.db_creds' 'module.db-connector.kubernetes_secret.db_creds'
# validate
terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars
```
I'll add a runbook with the exact sequence and backout steps.

arun: also add a note about lockfile regen (terraform providers.lock). when modules change provider constraints it can cause `terraform init -upgrade` diffs. recommend: create a staging plan with `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` pointing to a temp providers mirror or run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` and commit the new lockfile in the same PR.

sarah: good call. I will: - run `terraform providers lock` in staging - include the lockfile update in the module PR - include smoke plan in CI against the staging backend

javi: one more: secrets wiring for k8s apps — if we do migration job, apps can be updated to read both keys for a few deploys, then remove the legacy. add a feature flag or small compat layer in the deployment manifests.

liz: LGTM on process. small ask: tag infra-oncall and put a short ETA in the PR description so oncall knows the maintenance window. also add a link to the smoke plan output in the PR so reviewers can verify no resource replacements.

sarah: will do. target timeline: open PR now, run lockfile regen in staging tonight, run migration in staging tomorrow 02:00 UTC, then prod migration next Tue 03:00 UTC (if no regressions). tagging infra-oncall in the PR.

infra-bot: deploybot: created staging plan for branch `sarah/db-module-split` — plan url: https://ci.internal/redwood/plans/abc123 (expires in 48h)

arun: thanks — i'll review PR and validate the lockfile steps. ping me when the staging migration is done and i'll coordinate oncall for prod window. :thumbsup:
